newsitem.title: GERMANY: High ground water damages more E.German farmland.
newsitem.headline: High ground water damages more E.German farmland.

text.p: Farm work on 20,000 to 30,000 hectares of crop and grazing land in the eastern German state of Brandenburg has been made impossible because of high ground-water levels, the regional farm union (DBV) said.
This swamped acreage, unaccessible after two weeks of floods and heavy rain, had to be added to 15,000 hectares of farmland already totally submerged, a DBV spokesman told reporters on Friday.

Damages may now total up to one billion marks because farmers, apart from writing off this year's crops, would also be unable to plant any crops in the waterlogged fields for the 1998 harvest, he said.
As soon as the water recedes, experts need to assess whether toxic materials had been carried along by the Oder river floods, damaging the ground permanently.
Farmers who had used this year's crop as collateral against loans were threatened by financial ruin and this could not be offset by generous credit offers from the public sector.
The spokesman also gave latest livestock evacuation figures -- they included 25,000 beef cattle, 19,000 pigs and 4,000 sheep. --Vera Eckert, Hamburg newsroom, +49-40-41903275
